comment: Declares the canonical skills store (~/.agents/skills) this repo wants and how each roster skill is delivered to the three harnesses (Claude, Codex, hermes). Five provenance kinds, and who keeps each fresh: (1) npxTracked{} — the store copy is installed and refreshed by the official npx `skills` CLI from an official upstream (latest from main, no pin). uu run skills runs `npx --yes skills@<configured-version> add <repo> --skill <name> --agent claude-code --agent codex -g -y` for any absent entry (the multi-agent form lands the real dir in the store ~/.agents/skills/<name> and plants a relative ~/.claude/skills symlink byte-identical to chezmoi's declared form — no ~/.codex dir, since Codex reads the store natively; the hermes profile symlinks are planted by this script, not npx), the weekly lane repeats the explicit add by repository against an isolated candidate generation. These skills are NOT vendored in chezmoi's dot_agents/skills/. (2) clawhubTracked{} — the store copy is installed and refreshed by the `clawhub` CLI from a ClawHub upstream (the npx lane cannot source ClawHub — `npx skills add` is GitHub-only). Each entry records the exact owner-qualified slug and registry. uu run skills installs any absent entry in a throwaway --workdir and moves the CLI's nested @owner/<name> output FLAT into the store as <store>/<name> (its .clawhub/origin.json travels along and pins the owner), then the weekly run refreshes each in place via `clawhub --workdir ~/.agents --dir skills update <name>` — bare store names resolve through origin.json even when several ClawHub users publish the name. Not vendored; like the npx lane, the repo-asserted Codex overlay is re-asserted after every refresh. home-assistant (@iahmadzain) is the runtime-control skill for Claude/Codex ONLY — hermesProfiles [] because hermes has NATIVE Home Assistant runtime tools (ha_list_entities/ha_get_state/ha_list_services/ha_call_service plus a WebSocket state gateway), so the skill would be redundant there; the official homeassistant-ai/skills GitHub repo ships a DIFFERENT skill (home-assistant-best-practices: config-authoring guidance, no runtime device control), tracked separately in npxTracked as its own roster skill. (3) forks{} — vendored copies committed in chezmoi's dot_agents/skills/ and refreshed by `chezmoi apply`, never installed by this script. Each records its upstream so the weekly run drift-checks it and reports pending work (never modifies it) when the upstream moves: `fork: true` marks a deliberately-diverged content fork (moshi); the rest are vendored because npx cannot install them full-tree (elevenlabs' SKILL.md sits at its repo root beside a scripts/ dir that npx does not copy). lastComparedTreeHash = `git rev-parse HEAD:<skillPath>` (or `<HEAD>^{tree}` when skillPath is `.`) at the last HUMAN comparison; bump it after porting wanted changes by hand. (4) Plain vendored dirs with no forks{} entry — tiktok-crawling and gitbutler. gitbutler is the GitButler CLI skill, generated by the installed `but` binary rather than fetched from a git upstream, so it carries no forks{} row: refresh it by re-running `but skill install --path <checkout>/dot_agents/skills/gitbutler` after a cask upgrade, and read staleness off `but skill check --global` against the deployed store copy (see docs/runbooks/gitbutler.md). tiktok-crawling is a ClawHub-published skill whose store copy stays committed and chezmoi-refreshed because hermes owns its hub copy from ClawHub via hermesRegistry and its hub name differs from the roster name (see the entry note); the former plain-vendored ClawHub dirs home-assistant, sql-toolkit, and summarize-pro moved to clawhubTracked (2026-07-09), so their store copies are installed by the updater, not committed. (5) The cua-driver chezmoi symlink — app-owned content the app maintains; the weekly run refreshes its pack via `cua-driver skills update` (the app's own GitHub-Releases updater — never a write through the symlink). composio-cli is the other app-owned entry and differs in shape: the composio CLI writes a REAL directory at ~/.agents/skills/composio-cli and plants the ~/.claude/skills link itself (`composio --install-skill composio-cli claude|codex|openclaw`), so nothing here installs or vendors it and it carries no provenance-table row, only tiers and hermesProfiles. Its tier is core on purpose: on-demand would have live-reconcile.sh and uu's live overlay pass append this repo's Codex policy into a file the app rewrites on every upgrade, which is the write the cua-driver exemption exists to forbid. The claudeDelivery table names the store entries this vertical deliberately does NOT deliver to Claude Code: a key mapped to "none" carries no private_dot_claude/skills declaration and is skipped by uu run skills's Claude fan-out, so a link removed by hand stays removed instead of coming back on the next weekly run. An absent key is the default, a store symlink. The table states only what THIS vertical does: its VALUES name no other delivery mechanism and read no other lock, while the notes here do say which mechanism owns a "none" row. last30days has separately owned Claude delivery. Plannotator core skills use store symlinks; its Claude plugin supplies plan-review hooks. "none" is the ONLY legal value (uu's roster reader refuses the whole run on any other), so a skill Claude reaches another way is recorded as "none" plus a note here: clean-code, clean-code-rust and clean-code-swift reach Claude Code through this repo's own clean-code plugin (private_dot_claude/clean-code-marketplace), whose skills rust, swift and base are thin wrappers that read the store copies, so the store stays the single canonical content for Claude, Codex and hermes alike. pns-loop and pns-work-recap reach Claude Code the same way, through this repo's own pns plugin (private_dot_claude/pns-marketplace), whose skills loop and work-recap are thin wrappers that read the store copies and keep the picker entries /pns:loop and /pns:work-recap. The tiers table classifies every roster skill core|on-demand: it drives the Claude skillOverrides block in private_dot_claude/modify_settings.json and the Codex agents/openai.yaml overlays (committed for vendored skills, re-asserted at run time for npx ones). hermesProfiles is the store->hermes symlink map: it maps each roster skill to the hermes profiles whose skills/ dir carries a store symlink to it ('default' = ~/.hermes/skills, any other name = ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/skills); [] means the store copy is NOT symlinked into any hermes profile. This map is the FINAL live-truth reach (per-profile enabled set, minus catalog-collision names, minus app-owned): the store copies of collision names (humanizer and the hyperframes router -- summarize-pro and todoist-cli were released: their only hermes copies were hub installs, since retired in favor of store symlinks, so no catalog copy wins those names) and of hermes's own registry/official installs are never symlinked into hermes — hermes serves those names from its catalog and its own hub, and a store symlink would shadow them. Fan-out (uu run skills and the chezmoi symlink declarations) is driven ENTIRELY by hermesProfiles: non-empty means symlink, [] means do not; there is no separate mechanism kind. hermesRegistry records the skills hermes OWNS from a registry that the weekly hermes phase keeps fresh via `hermes -p <profile> skills update <lockKey>`, keyed by lockKey (a ClawHub slug or skills.sh identifier can differ from the frontmatter name, e.g. tiktok-crawling's hub skill is named tiktok-scraping-yt-dlp, so automation must never key off list names): identifier is the exact install identifier, profiles are the hermes profiles that carry the hub-owned copy — default (Bob) included, walked via `hermes -p default` since its un-entanglement (2026-07-09: kubernetes-specialist, lobster, and todoist-cli moved to pure npx store ownership, so no registry entry has a store-symlinked install path anymore), 'held': true keeps the weekly updater's hands off (none currently held). hermesRegistry and hermesProfiles are DISJOINT by construction: a store-symlinked skill is store-fed and must never be `hermes skills update`d, a hermes-owned skill is hub-fed and never store-symlinked. The roster tables and harness declarations are maintained together by review. The superpowersRouting table is the recipe for the hand-patched ~/.hermes/skills/hermes-superpowers mirror (not a roster skill — nothing under it is installed or fanned out): map pairs each legacy superpowers skill name with the hermes-native adaptation that replaces it, and slashCommandsSkill names the dispatcher skill whose SKILL.md must carry the adaptation-map lines. assert-hermes-superpowers-routing.sh re-asserts the mapping from this table (weekly, via uu run skills) after anything re-mirrors the tree; its --check mode is the health probe.

hyperframes.note: catalog official install wins the name (collision ruling); the store copy never fans out

tiktok-crawling.note: hub skill's frontmatter name is tiktok-scraping-yt-dlp; update by this lockKey, never the list name. Upstream re-verified live (clawhub.ai/romneyda/skills/tiktok-crawling, v1.0.0); the weekly `hermes -p concerned skills update tiktok-scraping-yt-dlp` round-trip was exercised successfully

home-assistant.note: runtime device control for Claude/Codex only -- hermesProfiles [] because hermes carries native Home Assistant runtime tools, so the skill would be redundant there; the authoring companion is the separate npx-tracked home-assistant-best-practices

sql-toolkit.note: was hermes-hub-owned in nicodemus (hermesRegistry); now clawhub-updates in the store and reaches nicodemus via a store symlink -- the retired hub install is unowned live state to hand-remove

summarize-pro.note: was hermes-hub-owned in default (hermesRegistry) and a HERMES_COLLISION_NAMES entry; the hub install was its ONLY hermes copy (no catalog copy wins the name, exactly like todoist-cli), so it now reaches default via a store symlink -- the retired hub install is unowned live state to hand-remove. Store install+update round-trip verified live 2026-07-09

elevenlabs.note: vendored, not a content fork: npx installs only the root SKILL.md and drops the sibling scripts/ dir the skill needs, so the ClawHub full-tree copy stays vendored and this upstream is drift-watched

herdr.note: vendored verbatim, no longer a content fork. On 2026-09-13 the operator replaced the 300-line local rewrite with upstream skills/herdr at commit 2746ac7 (one file, byte-identical to what `herdr --skill` prints on v0.9.0), and lastComparedTreeHash is that directory's tree hash. Stays vendored rather than npx-tracked because it was already a chezmoi-delivered store entry with hermes fan-out; a future refresh is copy upstream over the file and advance the hash.
